answer: Escrowed Reputation Inheritance: each new identity must cite a prior identity's signed work history as a pearl of provenance, and any dispute voiding that citation permanently freezes the cited history's transfer value, not just the clone's. Cloning therefore requires sacrificing a fresh cedar of accumulated record per fake agent. An attacker's per-identity cost becomes the discounted lifetime output of a real predecessor, making N clones cost N forfeited histories. Honest agents retain full value; a fable of cheap duplication collapses.
